title: The C++ solvers write the solution file and the sensors at the exact multiples of their write periods, interpolated within the step
author: Claude-JG
description: The C++ solvers write the solution file and the sensors at the end of the step that passes a multiple of the write period, so that the written times are not the multiples when the period is not a multiple of the step, and an adaptive step writes once for several periods. The Python solvers interpolate within the step since #3241. Decided (revision2026c step RG20.4.2, design advancedSolvers.md section 3.4): the dynamic C++ solvers write at each multiple of the write period within the step the state interpolated between the start and the end of the step - q by the cubic Hermite polynomial of q and q_t, q_t its derivative, the rest linear, the data coordinates of the end of the step, the coordinates of Lie group nodes linear - and restore the end of the step; a write period of 0 and the static solver write each step as before.
releaseNotes: The dynamic C++ solvers write the solution file and the sensors at the multiples of solution.file.writePeriod and solution.sensors.writePeriod and at the end; a write time within a step takes the state interpolated between the start and the end of the step (the ODE2 coordinates by the cubic Hermite polynomial of coordinates and velocities, the velocities by its derivative, the rest linear, Lie group nodes linear, the data coordinates of the end). A period that is a multiple of the step writes as before; a smaller period gives a row per period; 0 writes every step. Four test models changed by their output times; solverOutputWithinStepTest.py.
